rendered:
No. The document does not report comparing the method against PCR or blood culture on the clinical samples. Those techniques come up only in the introduction, which describes them as current standard methods:[1] bacterial culture [5] and polymerase chain reaction [6]are widely employed for pathogen identification; nevertheless, these techniques are often time-consuming and require specialized expertise[2].

For the clinical test, serum was collected from septic patients and healthy volunteers. The text describes the patients' infections only as septic patients with confirmed E. coli infection, septic patients with confirmed E. faecium infection[3]. It does not say how those infections were confirmed. The only result reported is that the sensor array's LDA plot showed well-resolved, non-overlapping clusters for the three tested serum groups[4] (see Fig. 5[5]). The points in that plot are technical replicates[6] of each serum sample, so no diagnostic accuracy was measured against a reference method. The main text gives no sensitivity, specificity or agreement figures against a reference test, and contains none of these terms:[7]. The full experimental procedures are said to be in the Supporting Information, which is not part of this document, so I can't confirm whether it includes such a comparison.
